findings.highlight: The narrative of her triumphant return to Japan would also be erased
findings.evidenceJa: 凱旋帰国の空気は一変し、冬馬家を取り巻く環境は、曜子さんが日本を追われた頃のように厳しくなるだろう。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts that the atmosphere of triumph will reverse and the actual environment surrounding the Touma family will become as harsh as when Youko was driven out of Japan. The English reduces renewed public and professional hostility to the erasure of a favorable 'narrative.'
findings.japanese:
凱旋帰国の空気は一変し、冬馬家を取り巻く環境は、
曜子さんが日本を追われた頃のように厳しくなるだろう。
findings.todokanai: The narrative of her triumphant return to Japan would also be erased, much like the time when Youko-san was ousted from Japan.

findings.highlight: Because she believes that Kazusa would be able to rise once more? Because she believes that Kazusa isn't someone so half-hearted that she would crumble over a scandal like this?
findings.evidenceJa:
必ず再起できるって。
この程度のスキャンダルで潰されるような
半端な実力ではないって。
findings.explanation: Youko trusts Kazusa's skill is not half-baked enough to be destroyed by this scandal; 'someone so half-hearted' shifts from ability to temperament — The claim that Kazusa's professional substance can survive the scandal remains.
findings.japanese:
必ず再起できるって。
この程度のスキャンダルで潰されるような
半端な実力ではないって。
findings.todokanai: Because she believes that Kazusa would be able to rise once more? Because she believes that Kazusa isn't someone so half-hearted that she would crumble over a scandal like this?

findings.highlight: "Just a little longer… please, just wait for one more day. I'm sure something's bound to happen."
findings.evidenceJa:
「もう少し…あと一日だけ待ってください。
絶対に何とかなりますから」
findings.explanation: Haruki promises they will definitely make something work; 'something's bound to happen' sounds passive and providential — His request for one more day and confidence are still explicit.
findings.japanese:
「もう少し…あと一日だけ待ってください。
絶対に何とかなりますから」
findings.todokanai: "Just a little longer… please, just wait for one more day. I'm sure something's bound to happen."

findings.highlight: This time… we will cast our final die.
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ…最後の賽が投げられた。
findings.explanation: The final die has just been cast: Youko has accepted Haruki's midnight deadline. The English moves the decisive act into the future, weakening the narration's explicit recognition that there is now no retreat.
findings.japanese:
今度こそ…
最後の賽が投げられた。
findings.todokanai: This time… we will cast our final die.

findings.highlight: after you decide whether or not you'll be going through with it
findings.evidenceJa: 「それを心配するのは、かずさがやるって決めた後だよ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says they will worry about the impossible production schedule after Kazusa decides that she will do it. The English changes the assumed affirmative decision into an open choice of whether or not, softening Setsuna's deliberate confidence and pressure.
findings.japanese:
「それを心配するのは、
かずさがやるって決めた後だよ」
findings.todokanai: "If I'm going to worry about that, it'll be only after you decide whether or not you'll be going through with it, Kazusa."

findings.highlight: You'll be able to enjoy yourself with many more people who will love you in this world
findings.evidenceJa: 「お母さんだけじゃなく、春希くんだけじゃない…もっとたくさんの、あなたを好きな人たちを、あなたの世界の中で、遊ばせてあげようよ？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna urges Kazusa to let many more people who love her come and play inside Kazusa's world. The English makes Kazusa the one enjoying herself with them, losing the proposed act of opening her formerly tiny world to others—the premise for Setsuna asking to be admitted again.
findings.japanese:
「お母さんだけじゃなく、春希くんだけじゃない…
もっとたくさんの、あなたを好きな人たちを、
あなたの世界の中で、遊ばせてあげようよ？」
findings.todokanai: "It won't be just your mother, and not just Haruki-kun either… You'll be able to enjoy yourself with many more people who will love you in this world, you know?"

findings.highlight: "After all, I, I… as long as Haruki stays by my side, I won't be able to give up on him! And as long as you stay by my side, Setsuna, I won't be able to stop envying you!"
findings.evidenceJa:
「だって、あたしは、あたしは…
春希の側にいる限り、あいつを諦めきれないよ！
雪菜の側にいる限り、お前を妬んじゃうんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she cannot give Haruki up as long as she remains beside him; 'as long as Haruki stays by my side' reverses who maintains the proximity — The impossible coexistence of the three remains.
findings.japanese:
「だって、あたしは、あたしは…
春希の側にいる限り、あいつを諦めきれないよ！
雪菜の側にいる限り、お前を妬んじゃうんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "After all, I, I… as long as Haruki stays by my side, I won't be able to give up on him! And as long as you stay by my side, Setsuna, I won't be able to stop envying you!"

findings.highlight: You won't be able to get into my world.
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前なんか、あたしの世界に入れてやらない。たとえ世界にお前とあたししかいなくても…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will not let Setsuna into her world even if only the two of them remain. The English turns an intentionally cruel refusal into Setsuna's inability to enter, removing Kazusa's agency immediately before she begs not to be excluded herself.
findings.japanese:
「お前なんか、あたしの世界に入れてやらない。
たとえ世界にお前とあたししかいなくても…」
findings.todokanai: "You won't be able to get into my world. Even if you and I are the only ones left in the world…"

findings.highlight: But now they're no longer with me… why were the two of them taken away from me!?
findings.evidenceJa: 「母さんとだって離れたくないよ…嫌だよ。たった二人しかいらないのに…どうして二人とも取り上げようとするんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she needs only two people—Haruki and her mother—and asks why the world is trying to take both away. The English says simply that the two are already gone, omitting the stark 'only those two' confession that answers Setsuna's invitation to fill her world with many people.
findings.japanese:
「母さんとだって離れたくないよ…嫌だよ。
たった二人しかいらないのに…
どうして二人とも取り上げようとするんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "I don't want to be separated from mom, either… I don't want that! But now they're no longer with me… why were the two of them taken away from me!?"

findings.highlight: I then proceed to slowly strum my fingers on the guitar, playing a melody I haven't listened to in a very long time.
findings.evidenceJa:
それからゆっくりと弦に指をかけて、
久しぶりの旋律を奏で始める。
findings.explanation: Haruki places his fingers on the strings and plays a melody he has not played in a long time; the English says he strums his fingers and has not listened to it — The next line explicitly identifies the two-year gap since he played this way.
findings.japanese:
それからゆっくりと弦に指をかけて、
久しぶりの旋律を奏で始める。
findings.todokanai: I then proceed to slowly strum my fingers on the guitar, playing a melody I haven't listened to in a very long time.

findings.highlight: With him playing outside like that, one could feel too embarrassed to even look.
findings.evidenceJa: 「…ちょっと、痛いでしょ？外からだと、恥ずかしくて見てられないかもね」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says Haruki's grand romantic guitar gesture is a little cringeworthy and may be too embarrassing to watch from an outsider's perspective. The English misreads 外から as Haruki physically playing outdoors, inventing a location and losing Setsuna's self-aware comment on how the scene looks to other people.
findings.japanese:
「…ちょっと、痛いでしょ？
外からだと、恥ずかしくて見てられないかもね」
findings.todokanai: "…It's a little awkward, isn't it? With him playing outside like that, one could feel too embarrassed to even look."

findings.highlight: The way I put it makes it sound like something made up
findings.evidenceJa: 「彼に凍らされた心を、彼が無理やり溶かしてくれた。…なんか、自作自演みたいな言い方だけど、それが実際、二年前にあったこと」
findings.explanation: Setsuna jokes that Haruki freezing her heart and then forcibly thawing it sounds like 自作自演—creating the crisis and staging its solution himself. The English says only that it sounds fictitious, discarding the pointed joke about Haruki being both culprit and rescuer.
findings.japanese:
「彼に凍らされた心を、彼が無理やり溶かしてくれた。
…なんか、自作自演みたいな言い方だけど、
それが実際、二年前にあったこと」
findings.todokanai: "My heart was frozen by him, but he also forcibly melted it… The way I put it makes it sound like something made up, but it actually happened two years ago."

findings.highlight: Perhaps you think that the best way to save you would be to not get involved with you.
findings.evidenceJa: 「本当なら、わたしがいないことが、あなたにとって一番の救いなのかもしれない」
findings.explanation: Setsuna admits that, in truth, her complete absence may be the greatest salvation for Kazusa. The English instead attributes the idea to Kazusa and reduces absence to Setsuna merely not getting involved, weakening the sacrifice that Setsuna immediately says she cannot make.
findings.japanese:
「本当なら、わたしがいないことが、
あなたにとって一番の救いなのかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "Perhaps you think that the best way to save you would be to not get involved with you."
